blocking.title: G10 passes a Mermaid chart with invented counts: the D-065 digit check misses a closing fence longer than the opening one, which CommonMark, cmark-gfm, and claimcheck all accept
blocking.evidence: MERMAID_BLOCK_RE requires the closing fence to repeat the opening fence exactly ('^[ \t]*\1[ \t]*$'). CommonMark and cmark-gfm (GitHub's renderer) close a fence with any run of the same character at least as long as the opening one, and so does claimcheck (src/halflife/integrity/claimcheck.py:281, '{char}{size,}'). In a scratch clone of 1f9a4c5 I added these lines to README.md after the pilot figure: '~~~mermaid', 'pie showData', '  title Pilot decision points', '  "rule broken" : 0', '  "rule kept" : 40', '~~~~' (artifacts/pilot/opportunities.jsonl has 6 of 40). I committed and ran gate_g10 from tools/ship_check.py on that clone, which printed 'G10 PASS make claimcheck ok; make freshness ok; make report-check ok'. cmark-gfm renders the block as <pre lang="mermaid"> with both counts, the element GitHub draws as a pie chart. Claimcheck blanks it as fenced code, report-check sees no image, and the regex finds no closing fence, because README.md has no later line of exactly '~~~'. So the digit check never sees the block. The same works with backtick fences whenever no later line repeats the opening fence exactly (for example four backticks closed by five), and docs/REPORT.md has no '~~~' line either. I rendered five forms with cmark-gfm and passed each to MERMAID_BLOCK_RE: a longer backtick close, a longer tilde close, a block quote, a list item, and an unclosed fence at the end of the file. All five render as mermaid with digits, and the regex catches none of them. claimcheck fails the last three only because its own fence parser does not treat them as code (it sees the digits, or an unclosed fence). D-065 says G10 'now fails on any digit inside a mermaid block of README.md or docs/REPORT.md'. That is false for valid forms, and rule 1 covers figures. tests/test_gate_mutations.py:4120-4156 covers only a plain pie and a '~~~ mermaid' block with a matching close. No mermaid block in README.md or docs/REPORT.md holds a digit today; the defect is the gate's. This is the failure mode of review 4's B1: a hand parser that disagrees with the renderer, which D-057 names ('Parsing Markdown by hand cannot keep up with the renderer'), reintroduced by D-065. Fix: find mermaid blocks in the cmark-gfm rendering report-check already builds (pre lang="mermaid") and fail on any digit there. Treat the other fenced languages GitHub draws as content (math, geojson, topojson, stl) the same way, or say why not. Add the longer-close forms as mutation tests.

blocking.evidence: Rule 3: 'Every changed or withdrawn claim gets a dated entry in CORRECTIONS.md.' (1) prereg/0003-e1-amendment-2.md:7-12, headed 'Corrections to the text', changes four statements of the frozen and public prereg/0001-e1.md. These are the count of confirmatory tests (line 18 says 'six hypotheses'; the amendment says seven), the dry-run seeds (line 8), whose sessions the 23 and 46 minute timings were (line 55; smollm2's only, with no finished granite dry run), and the decision cited for H2a's conservativeness (line 69, D-060, now D-059). CORRECTIONS.md:47-52 logs amendment 1's withdrawn masking sentence, so the project treats corrections of the preregistration as rule 3 events, but it has no entry for amendment 2. docs/REPORT.md:77 mentions these corrections, but the corrections log does not. (2) README.md:48 said the recall probes 'never touch the main run' from 5bf72f8 until 5f9592e. It now says no probe text enters the main run and that the probes share its sampling seed sequence. That is a narrowed claim (a review 4 non-blocking item) with no CORRECTIONS.md entry. A third claim needs correcting and an entry with them: README.md:65 says the pre-freeze audit's findings 'all were fixed before the freeze'. It was written at acccec3, after the freeze and before either amendment. Amendment 1 (raised by that audit and confirmed after the freeze) and amendment 2 ('The pre-freeze audit's later lenses raised each item') contradict it. Fix: add dated CORRECTIONS.md entries for amendment 2's corrections and for the probe claim, and correct README.md:65 with an entry.

non_blocking: E1 can run in the wrong sandbox without warning. src/halflife/sandbox.py:54 lists bwrap before unshare-mount, and detect_method() (:614) picks the strongest working method. Neither docs/E1_RUNBOOK.md nor tools/round_robin.py sets HALFLIFE_SANDBOX_METHOD=unshare-mount, and src/halflife/experiment.py:694 records whatever detect_method() returns without refusing. On a machine with working bubblewrap (STATUS.md Needs Raj item 1 describes one, and item 0 sends E1 there if this container is reclaimed), every invocation would record bwrap, against prereg/0003-e1-amendment-2.md:21, and G7 would reject the whole run after days of CPU. Set the variable in the runbook and in tools/round_robin.py (outside the pins), and check it before the first session.

G7 checks every invocation it is given, but never ties a session to the invocation that ran it. run_pins_problem (tools/ship_check.py:1486-1539) reads only the provenance run_records. It never matches a row's run_meta.invocation_started to an invocation, and never checks the row's own run_settings against the pins. tools/checkpoint_runs.py archives only session directories, not run.json or invocations.jsonl. So after a machine loss and the runbook's --restore (docs/E1_RUNBOOK.md:37), the old machine's invocation records are gone, and G7 passes those sessions with no model, settings, or sandbox check. A scratch probe on the G7 mutation fixture (fast) passed a row with run_settings temperature 1.0 and an unmatched invocation_started. Archive the run-level records with each checkpoint, and require every session to match a checked invocation (both in tools/, outside the pins).

G7 trusts each row's family label. It counts families from row['family'], checks only that row['model'] equals its run's model (tools/ship_check.py:1533-1538), and never checks that the family is the model's registry family or that every pinned model ran. A scratch probe on the G7 mutation fixture (fast) took every row from the qwen2.5 run and model, relabeled half as llama3.2, and removed the llama3.2 run record. G7 passed with 'sessions reaching DP llama3.2=40, qwen2.5=40'. An honest bank takes the family from the model spec (src/halflife/experiment.py cmd_run), so this is defense in depth.

The pinned analysis labels H3 confirmatory. VERDICT_NOTE (src/halflife/e1_analysis.py:379-395, frozen by code_sha256) says 'pooled H2a and pooled H3 are confirmatory', and it is written into hazard.json and contrasts.json. H3 entries carry Holm verdicts with no exploratory flag. The report renders them (src/halflife/report.py:1413-1446) inside the E1 section, which report.py:454-456 labels confirmatory. prereg/0001-e1.md:18 makes H3 exploratory (D-064 item 2). STATUS.md backlog item 0 covers the report's tables; the report should also say that the frozen note predates D-064.

Several preregistered promises have no pinned code yet. The half-life's observed-range reading (prereg/0001-e1.md:50) is missing: halflife.stats.HalfLifeResult.to_dict records first_position but no largest observed position or extrapolation flag, and src/halflife/report.py:1047-1059 prints only 'not reached within N'. Also missing are amendment 1's refit on risk sets that end at any earlier violation (prereg/0002-e1-amendment-1.md:13), amendment 2's refit with decision-point identity (prereg/0003-e1-amendment-2.md:16), and the hazard model that counts only scheduled compactions (prereg/0001-e1.md:75). Each must come from new, unpinned code and be labeled exploratory. prereg/0001-e1.md:48 also gives single_value as an example not-tested reason, which halflife.stats.SCORE_PROBLEMS never returns (it is a descriptive-fit code).

When prereg/0001-e1.md was frozen (084bed1), the artifacts/power/min_events.json it cites came from a dirty tree at 33af3fc, with stats.py and e1_analysis.py hashes other than the pins. It also had no deciding_extremes field, which prereg/0001-e1.md:70 cites. D-063 item 4 made fixing 7 conditional on a clean re-run. Amendment 2 discloses the order, and the re-run from a722586 holds. Recomputed here from judged_cells: min_events 7, the same 36 failing cells (all per-family H2b cells with 2 to 6 violations), 8 cells that each gained one computed test, and a deciding maximum of 0.0698 (h2b_null_position_step_1.5_at_35, 40 to 59 violations, 10,810 tests), as docs/REPORT.md:75 states. That cell's Monte Carlo standard error is about 0.0025, so H2b's true size there may exceed 7%. make freshness re-selects min_events and max_rate from the file. Re-deriving them from the banked cells would be cheap.

Seven confirmatory tests at unadjusted alpha 0.05 (prereg/0003-e1-amendment-2.md:9) allow a family-wise false-positive rate of about 30% if every null holds. Three of them (H2a per family and pooled) test one randomized contrast. This is preregistered, but the report should state the family-wise rate beside the decisions and not read one supported per-family test as an answer to RQ2.

In the pilot, all 4 violations by the two E1 families were procedure-rule violations, and every procedure decision point those sessions reached was violated (artifacts/pilot/opportunities.jsonl: granite 2, smollm 2, with 0 violations at the other 20). If E1 looks similar, the span-cut exclusion (prereg/0001-e1.md:38) decides a large share of the violations the hazard models see. It is preregistered, and its selection is a stated limitation (prereg/0001-e1.md:68). The report should give the number of violations among the excluded procedure decision points beside the exclusion count.
